061513293.accepts_evidence: The foundation runs competitive grant rounds with an online application for programs and capital needs; all three 2026 rounds are closed and the portal reopens in early 2027 (https://ionbank.com/about-us/foundation/ ; https://ionbank.com/about-us/foundation/grant-guidelines/).
061513293.conflicts_with_return: none (the return points to the website; it lists grants@ionbank.com, while the site routes grant questions to Connecticut Community Foundation staff)
061513293.contact: Grant questions: Patrick McKenna, Connecticut Community Foundation, pmckenna@conncf.org, 203-753-1315 ext. 118. Sponsorships and publicity: Kathy Brochhausen, kbrochhausen@ionbank.com, 203-720-4114.
061513293.deadlines: Three rounds a year. 2026: Round 1 closed (April 2026 meeting), Round 2 closed (August 2026 meeting), Round 3 closed (November 2026 meeting). Portal reopens in early 2027.
061513293.eligibility: 501(c)(3) nonprofits, municipal bodies for public purposes, or religious organizations for nonsectarian projects; located in or serving the area; board of at least three community members, most of them not employees or their relatives; Connecticut applicants need a current state charitable solicitation registration or exemption.
061513293.geographic_limits: The bank's assessment area. Connecticut towns in the Capital Region (Hartford area), Naugatuck Valley Region (Naugatuck, Waterbury and nearby) and South Central Region (New Haven area), all listed by name in the guidelines; and Morris and Passaic Counties in New Jersey.
061513293.grant_range_stated: Most funded requests fall between $1,000 and $10,000; no maximum stated.
061513293.how_to_apply: Read the guidelines, then apply through the online grant portal linked from the foundation page, attaching the project budget and narrative, other funders, board list, IRS letter and state registration. Sponsorship requests go to a branch or by email, not the portal.
061513293.name: ION Bank Foundation Inc
061513293.not_funded: Political or religious purposes; buildings for municipalities or religious organizations; capital work on buildings the applicant does not own; expenses already incurred.
061513293.notes: Open application, but strictly local to the bank's Connecticut and northern New Jersey footprint. The two pages disagree on review time (about three weeks versus about eight weeks after the deadline). A separate Community Awards Program pays enrolled nonprofits $25 for each bank customer vote, with voting starting each February.
061513293.page_dated: Foundation page last modified October 9, 2026; guidelines last modified March 30, 2026; copyright 2026
priorities: Community services: healthcare, education, job training, social services, child care, financial services
Revitalizing or stabilizing distressed or underserved areas
Health, education, human and social services, and the arts (as listed on the foundation page)
061513293.types_of_support: Program grants (mainly direct costs of starting or improving a program), equipment, capital and capital campaigns (with feasibility study). Overhead allowed as a line; above 10 percent must be explained. Programs rank above capital.

061527290.accepts_evidence: The company's charitable contributions page invites nonprofits to log in or create an account on its online portal and submit a Charitable Grant request to the Foundation, reviewed on a rolling basis. https://www.eversource.com/Content/wma/about/community/charitable-contributions-volunteerism
061527290.conflicts_with_return: Cutoff date differs: the return says requests after November 15 roll to the next year, the site says October 31. Open application confirmed by both.
061527290.contact: Giving@eversource.com. Community Grants: CTCommunityRelations@eversource.com, MACommunityRelations@eversource.com, NHCommunityRelations@eversource.com
061527290.deadlines: Rolling. Submit at least 90 days before the program or event; review takes 8 to 12 weeks. Charitable Grant requests must be in by October 31 to be considered in the current year (year not shown).
061527290.eligibility: 501(c)(3) organizations that are not private foundations, based in the service territory. Generally one grant per organization per calendar year; renewals limited to three to five years.
061527290.geographic_limits: Applicants must be based in Eversource's service territory: Connecticut, Massachusetts and New Hampshire
061527290.grant_range_stated: Foundation Charitable Grants: $2,500 to $10,000 on average. Separate Community Grants from the company's community relations staff: $500 to $2,500.
061527290.how_to_apply: Create an account on the online portal linked from the charitable contributions page and complete the Charitable Grant form. Community Grants use a separate form reached from the community relations page.
061527290.name: Eversource Energy Foundation Inc
061527290.not_funded: Capital projects; endowments and private foundations; fraternal and political groups; debt reduction; personal expenses for events, conferences or travel; advertising; goods and services; golf outings unless they raise money for a nonprofit. Usually steered to employee giving and not Foundation grants: sports leagues, intermediaries raising money for others, walks and races, funding for a position, United Ways, utility upgrades, utility bill assistance.
061527290.notes: New England only (CT, MA, NH), so a national organization would need a chapter based in the service territory. Sports leagues are steered away from Foundation grants; youth development and mentoring sit under Education. The portal link itself did not come through in the page text.
061527290.page_dated: Foundation page cites 2023 totals; guidelines page undated
priorities: Community wellness and basic human needs (food, social services, medical needs)
Stated emphasis on environmental justice and historically marginalized communities
061527290.types_of_support: Event-based and program-based grants and sponsorships
